title: Numeric Ranges
question: Is the numeric range constraint present at each capture boundary?
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.
why: Without bounds a downstream model may request out-of-range values.

notes.crewai: CrewAI: preserved inside the `anyOf` wrapper emitted for optional fields, so the constraint sits one level down rather than being lost.
notes.llamaindex: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `McpToolSpec` rebuilds each `inputSchema` as a Pydantic model (`create_model_from_json_schema`), and the model's JSON schema is what `ToolMetadata.to_openai_tool` hands the LLM. Fields become plain `int`/`float` with no constraints, so `minimum` and `maximum` are dropped.
notes.google_adk_js: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: `MCPTool._getDeclaration` passes `inputSchema` through `toGeminiSchema`, which keeps `type`, `description`, `enum`, `items`, `properties`, `required` and `anyOf` in the genai `Schema` dialect; `minimum` and `maximum` are not among them, so `limit`'s bounds and `max_words.minimum` are dropped.
notes.copilot_sdk: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): `minimum` and `maximum` are removed from the provider schema and appended to the parameter description as text, e.g. `{minimum: 1, maximum: 100}` on `limit`.
notes.langchain4j: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: `McpToolProvider` maps each `inputSchema` into LangChain4j's own `JsonSchemaElement` model (`JsonObjectSchema`, `JsonStringSchema`, `JsonIntegerSchema`, ...), and the `ToolSpecification` AiServices hands the `ChatModel` is built from that model. `JsonIntegerSchema` and `JsonNumberSchema` hold a description only, so `minimum` and `maximum` are dropped.
notes.koog: Koog 1.3.0-beta: `minimum` and `maximum` are dropped: `ToolParameterType.Integer` has no range slot, so `limit` (1 to 100) and `max_words` reach the model as bare integers.

summary: A framework that rebuilds the input schema from its own model class can drop the bounds. Where a framework builds its schema from a model class, optional parameters are wrapped, and a constraint that stays inside the wrapper counts as present.
